name: Alabama
taxNotes: Alabama uses graduated individual income-tax brackets. Some municipalities also impose occupational taxes.

name: Alaska
taxNotes: Alaska has no state income tax on wages.

name: Arizona
taxNotes: Arizona uses a flat state income-tax rate. Employees elect a withholding percentage on Form A-4.

name: Arkansas
taxNotes: Arkansas uses graduated individual income-tax brackets. The withholding amount depends on your income level.
taxAgency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration

name: California
taxNotes: California uses graduated income-tax brackets and withholds State Disability Insurance (SDI) separately.

name: Colorado
taxNotes: Colorado uses a flat individual income-tax rate. Paid family and medical leave (FAMLI) contributions may also appear on your paycheck.

name: Connecticut
taxNotes: Connecticut uses graduated income-tax brackets. Employees must select a CT-W4 withholding code.

name: Delaware
taxNotes: Delaware uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding tables and Form W-4 elections apply.

name: District of Columbia
taxNotes: DC uses graduated income-tax brackets. Withholding is based on Form D-4 elections.
taxAgency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue

name: Florida
taxNotes: Florida does not impose a broad individual state income tax on wages.

name: Georgia
taxNotes: Georgia uses a flat individual income-tax structure. Payroll results can vary with allowances, deductions, and credits.

name: Hawaii
taxNotes: Hawaii uses graduated income-tax brackets with rates that increase with income.

name: Idaho
taxNotes: Idaho uses a flat individual income-tax rate. Withholding is affected by your Idaho Form ID W-4 elections.

name: Illinois
taxNotes: Illinois uses a flat individual income-tax structure. Exemptions and credits can make withholding differ from a simple percentage.

name: Indiana
taxType: flat state income tax (3.05%) plus county tax
taxNotes: Indiana uses a flat state income tax, and most counties impose an additional county income tax based on your residence or work location.

name: Iowa
taxNotes: Iowa uses a flat income-tax rate. Taxable wages and withholding elections on Form IA W-4 affect the amount withheld.

name: Kansas
taxNotes: Kansas uses graduated income-tax brackets. State-specific withholding tables and Form K-4 elections apply.

name: Kentucky
taxNotes: Kentucky uses a flat state income tax. Some cities and counties also impose occupational or payroll taxes.

name: Louisiana
taxNotes: Louisiana uses graduated income-tax brackets. State-specific withholding rules and Form L-4 elections apply.

name: Maine
taxNotes: Maine uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding is based on Form W-4ME elections.

name: Maryland
taxType: graduated state income tax plus county tax
taxNotes: Maryland combines graduated state income tax with county-level income tax. Your county of residence significantly affects your total withholding.

name: Massachusetts
taxType: flat income tax (5%) plus high-earner surtax
taxNotes: Massachusetts uses a flat wage-tax rate of 5%, with an additional 4% surtax on income above $1 million.

name: Michigan
taxNotes: Michigan uses a flat state income tax. Certain cities, including Detroit, impose separate city income taxes.

name: Minnesota
taxNotes: Minnesota uses graduated withholding brackets. The 2026 Paid Leave program premium may also be withheld separately.

name: Mississippi
taxNotes: Mississippi uses a flat income-tax rate. State withholding depends on your Form 89-350 elections.

name: Missouri
taxNotes: Missouri uses graduated income-tax brackets. Kansas City and St. Louis also impose earnings taxes.

name: Montana
taxNotes: Montana uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding tables and Form MW-4 elections apply.

name: Nebraska
taxNotes: Nebraska uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding tables and Form W-4N elections apply.

name: Nevada
taxNotes: Nevada does not impose a broad individual state income tax on wages.

name: New Hampshire
taxNotes: New Hampshire does not impose an income tax on wages or salaries.
taxAgency: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration

name: New Jersey
taxNotes: New Jersey uses graduated income-tax brackets and may withhold separate employee contributions for state benefit programs.

name: New Mexico
taxNotes: New Mexico uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding is based on your income level and Form W-4 elections.
taxAgency: New Mexico Taxation and Revenue Department

name: New York
taxNotes: New York uses graduated income-tax brackets. NYC and Yonkers residents may face additional local income tax withholding.
taxAgency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance

name: New York City
taxType: NYC resident tax (3.078%–3.876%) plus NY state tax
taxNotes: NYC residents pay both New York State income tax and New York City resident income tax.
taxAgency: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance

name: North Carolina
taxNotes: North Carolina uses a flat income-tax rate. Standard deductions and allowances reduce taxable wages.

name: North Dakota
taxNotes: North Dakota uses graduated income-tax brackets with relatively low rates.
taxAgency: North Dakota Office of State Tax Commissioner

name: Ohio
taxType: graduated income tax plus local taxes
taxNotes: Ohio uses graduated income-tax brackets, and many municipalities and school districts impose separate local income taxes.

name: Oklahoma
taxNotes: Oklahoma uses graduated income-tax brackets. State-specific withholding tables and Form OK-W-4 elections apply.

name: Oregon
taxNotes: Oregon uses graduated income-tax brackets. Statewide transit tax and paid-leave contributions may appear separately.

name: Pennsylvania
taxNotes: Pennsylvania uses a flat state income tax. Municipalities and school districts may also impose local earned-income taxes.

name: Rhode Island
taxNotes: Rhode Island uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding is based on Form RI W-4 elections.

name: South Carolina
taxNotes: South Carolina uses graduated income-tax brackets. Allowances and standard deductions reduce taxable wages.

name: South Dakota
taxNotes: South Dakota does not impose a state income tax on wages.

name: Tennessee
taxType: no state income tax on wages
taxNotes: Tennessee does not impose a broad individual income tax on wage income.

name: Texas
taxNotes: Texas has no state income tax. Federal taxes and employee benefits still reduce take-home pay.

name: Utah
taxNotes: Utah uses a flat individual income-tax structure. Withholding is affected by current state forms and tax credits.

name: Vermont
taxNotes: Vermont uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding is based on Form W-4VT elections.

name: Virginia
taxNotes: Virginia uses graduated income-tax brackets. State-specific withholding tables and Form VA-4 elections apply.

name: Washington
taxType: no state income tax on wages
taxNotes: Washington does not impose a broad individual income tax on wages, but paid-leave and long-term-care payroll contributions may apply.

name: West Virginia
taxNotes: West Virginia uses graduated income-tax brackets. State withholding is based on Form WV/IT-104 elections.

name: Wisconsin
taxNotes: Wisconsin uses graduated individual income-tax brackets. State-specific withholding tables and Form WT-4 elections apply.

name: Wyoming
taxNotes: Wyoming does not impose a state income tax on wages.
